details:
ARES-1 Outpost Trainer — Deep Space Habitat Simulator

1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

ARES-1 Outpost Trainer is an interactive, browser-based life-support trade-off simulator designed for young explorers (ages 7–12) answering the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players step into the shoes of Flight Director for humanity’s first permanent outpost on the Moon (Shackleton Crater) or Mars (Jezero Crater).

Each sol (mission day), the player manages a limited power grid across four interconnected subsystems:

  • Life Support: Drives oxygen generation and catalytic CO₂ scrubbers.
  • Radiation Mass Shielding: Powers the interior storm shelter to absorb cosmic rays and solar particles.
  • Hydroponics Bay: Cultivates fresh greens under LED lighting, generating food, supplementary O₂, and crew morale.
  • Thermal Control: Heats the habitat against freezing -173°C lunar nights and -60°C Martian chill.

Before committing a turn, players see a live "Causal Impact Preview" that reveals the consequences of their power choices. Over 10 sols, they must navigate 8 randomized crisis events (Coronal Mass Ejections, dust storms, water recycler biofilm, and thermal radiator leaks).

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

Most educational space content for children stays abstract (posters or passive trivia) without conveying the core reality of spaceflight: no choice is free. ARES-1 bridges this gap by turning genuine engineering constraints into playful mechanics:

  • Kids learn systems thinking—saving power on heating freezes crops, while starving life support builds toxic CO₂.
  • It demystifies real aerospace trade-offs in plain, kid-friendly English.
  • Being 100% web-based with zero installs or accounts, it is instantly accessible to classrooms, STEM clubs, and families worldwide on mobile, tablet, or desktop.

3. Tools, Coding Languages & Tech Stack

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, and Vite 6 for high-performance client-side execution.
  • Styling & Design System: Tailwind CSS v4 (@tailwindcss/vite) with custom space-age animations.
  • UI Icons: Lucide React.
  • Procedural Sound Engine: Native Web Audio API (AudioContext) generating real-time radio chirps, warning alarms, and victory fanfares without external audio files.
  • Testing: Vitest test suite with 15 automated unit and balance simulation tests ensuring rigorous, fair gameplay math.
  • Deployment: Hosted continuously on Netlify and GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions CI/CD.

4. Creativity & Innovation

  • 100% Inline Procedural SVG Graphics: The habitat visualizer is crafted entirely in code—featuring dynamic solar panel dust accumulation that players can manually brush off via EVA, responsive radiation shield bubbles, greenhouse harvest animations, and an interactive rover soil scanner.
  • RoboCapcom Mentor: An inline SVG robot advisor that analyzes the player's telemetry in real time and provides tactical advice without spoiling solutions.
  • Post-Mission Debrief & Sparklines: When the mission concludes, players receive a flight evaluation with SVG telemetry sparklines, failure-chain post-mortems, and earned rank badges.

5. Real NASA Open Data & Science Grounding

Rather than inventing fictional parameters, our simulation connects directly to verified NASA open datasets:

  • NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database): Connects to api.nasa.gov/DONKI to query live Coronal Mass Ejections and solar flares, dynamically scaling in-game radiation risk based on current real-world solar conditions.
  • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR): Incorporates findings from study OSD-100 (astronaut cellular DNA damage from deep space radiation) and OSD-37 (GeneLab microgravity plant photosynthesis efficiency).
  • NASA Marshall Space Flight Center ECLSS: Models real 98% closed-loop water recovery and Sabatier reactor CO₂ catalytic scrubbing.
  • NASA Artemis & Mars Perseverance MEDA: Grounds lunar South Pole thermal swings (+120°C in sunlight to -173°C in shadow) and Jezero Crater atmospheric dust opacity.
